recap:

1. find a trigger
2. stack a good one + a bad one
3. make something before you email
4. pick a framework: label, loss, gift, open loop, peer mirror

timing first. copy second.

bookmark this and follow for more.

the peer mirror only works if the peers are similar.

don't compare a local cafe to starbucks.

don't compare a 20-person startup to nike.

same market. same size. same stage.

that's what makes them feel behind.

example (local marketing):

"hey dr. patel, noticed a few dentists near you started posting short FAQ videos on their google profile. yours doesn't have any yet. i wrote 3 scripts you could shoot in an afternoon. lemme know if i can send them?"

framework 5: the peer mirror

show them what businesses like theirs are already doing.

template:

"hey [name], noticed a few [businesses like theirs] started [doing the thing]. you haven't yet. i put together [what you made] so you can try it. want it?"

why the open loop works:

the first tip proves you know what you're talking about.

now they want the second one.

curiosity does the selling for you.

example (SEO):

"hey rachel, spent some time on your blog and i think i found two reasons traffic's been dipping. the first one's easy. none of your posts link to each other. the second one's in your titles and it's a bit bigger. want me to walk you through it?"

framework 4: the open loop

give them one thing for free. keep the second one.

template:

"hey [name], spent some time on [their thing] and found two things. the first one's easy: [problem one]. the second one's a bit bigger. want me to walk you through it?"

example (copywriting):

"hey leo, saw your reddit post asking people to roast your landing page. most people went after the design, but honestly i think it's the headline. i took a shot at rewriting it. want to see it?"

framework 3: the gift

you skip the pitch and just hand them the work.

template:

"hey [name], saw [where you found them]. most people said [the obvious answer], but honestly i think it's [the actual issue]. took a shot at fixing it. want to see?"

example (email marketing):

"hey jordan, i added the wool jacket to my cart last week and forgot about it. never heard from you after. 

pretty sure that's happening with a lot of carts. 

i wrote a quick 3-email reminder flow using your own product copy. can I send it?"
